subject.title: [Feature]: Start and persist routed agent sessions from outbound WhatsApp sends

question: Should outbound `openclaw message send` infer the routed agent from channel/account/peer bindings automatically when no agent or session is explicit, or require an explicit opt-in flag or command before mirroring into an agent session?
rationale: Both behaviors are plausible product contracts: automatic inference matches inbound routing and the reported workflow, while an explicit opt-in avoids changing the meaning of existing channel-only outbound sends.

options.title: Infer routed agent when unambiguous
options.body: Use account/peer route bindings for outbound sends only after preserving explicit agent and session precedence, and add shared tests across CLI and message-tool/Gateway paths.

options.title: Require explicit opt-in
options.body: Add a flag or dedicated command for session-aware outbound starts so existing `message send` remains channel-only unless the operator asks to mirror into a session.

options.title: Keep outbound sends channel-only
options.body: Document the current behavior and require users to start the routed agent session separately before or after sending the opener.

recommendation.title: Infer routed agent when unambiguous
recommendation.body: Use account/peer route bindings for outbound sends only after preserving explicit agent and session precedence, and add shared tests across CLI and message-tool/Gateway paths.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision centers on the outbound session routing/plugin boundary that this history most directly touched.
